messages:
maria: Quick bring-up for slowburn-13b (public checkpoint) — ran quant sweep + smoke eval on GTN product slice. TL;DR: int8 looks cost-neutral vs our prod baseline but slightly slower; int4 is materially cheaper but has non-trivial quality drop on long-form GTN prompts. I put a short recommendation at the bottom.

sam: can you post the numbers (latency/p95, delta vs baseline, and unit cost) and the eval prompts you used?

maria: sure — paste of the quick table below: 
```
baseline (opt-13b-int8 prod): p50 210ms, p95 480ms, ROUGE-L (GTN slice) 68.5, cost ~ $0.92 / 1k tokens
slowburn-13b-int8: p50 230ms (+10%), p95 520ms (+8%), ROUGE-L 69.1 (+0.6), cost ~ $0.65 / 1k tokens
slowburn-13b-int4: p50 200ms (-5%), p95 450ms (-6%), ROUGE-L 65.7 (-2.8), cost ~ $0.45 / 1k tokens
kv-cache cold-warm diff: int4 cold p95 spikes +150ms on first token for some prompts (priming-heavy).
```
maria: eval artifacts: run id run/2026-03-slowburn-quant, 1.5k GTN prompts (mix of short/long), live traffic parity slice ~2% of prod. full logs in the eval bucket (link redacted).

lee: high level econ view — int4 saves ~30-35% per-token vs slowburn-int8, ~50% vs baseline. If product accepts a 2.8 ROUGE-L drop on the GTN slice, breakeven is immediate; if not, consider hybrid routing. For our margins, 20% routing to int4 yields ~6-8% unit cost reduction for the overall product while keeping WPS (word-preservation signal) regression <1.0 on sample checks. Recommend a staged canary: 5% -> 20% -> 50% with automated signal gating.

alex: GTN/product perspective: major customers care about long-form quality more than small savings. We need a clear signal set to gate int4 traffic: (1) ROUGE-L delta per prompt class, (2) hallucination rate on factual prompts, (3) human QA fail rate on top-10% rated outputs. If int4 fails any gate, fallback to int8. Also request a small manual QA cohort for the 20% stage.

taylor: infra notes — int4 increases batchability so throughput per GPU improves, but we saw the kv-cache cold spike for long prompts. Ops suggestions: enable aggressive prefix caching in the canary region, and pin int4 instances to a region with low cold-start variability. Also set autoscale headroom +25% for the first 48h of the canary.

sam: for the experiment, propose metrics and thresholds: 
```
- sample size: 5k live requests over 48h per stage
- thresholds: ROUGE-L mean delta <= -0.7, hallucination rate delta <= +1.0%, human QA fail <= +2.0%
- rollback: any threshold breached for 3 consecutive windows (15m) -> auto rollback
```

alex: product okay with staged hybrid if the human QA cohort signs off at 20%. please add a prompt set that emphasizes long-form coherence and multi-step reasoning.

maria: my operational rec: start canary int4 @5% for 48h, run live eval hooks + synthetic prompts, if stable -> expand 20% for 72h with manual QA (5 reviewers, blind). If still stable, keep 20% as a persistent mixed-fleet routing for low-sensitivity GTN flows and route high-sensitivity flows to int8 only. Also add a per-customer opt-out flag.

deploy-bot: canary created: canary/slowburn-13b-int4-5pct at 3313370060. Logs streaming to /canaries/slowburn-13b-int4/3313370060. :rocket:

lee: one more econ note — report weekly cost delta to finance: show realized tokens on int4 vs int8, and carry forward quality uplift/decline. If int4 improvements in RLHF / decoding tweaks recover 1.5-2 pts of ROUGE, we can re-evaluate wider rollout.

maria: thanks all — I'll queue the canary + attach the GTN long-form prompt set. Will post first 24h snapshot in this thread.
